reviews.title: Disgusting customer service
reviews.text: Avoid this app. I have been left disgusted and distraught at my treatment from a company that is geared towards people’s well being. I signed up on a free trial, I was doing the workouts and actually enjoyed doing, so no problems there. However, when the time came to renew my membership, my financial situation had dramatically changed meaning I could not afford to renew. The renewal had not been taken from my account so I cancelled my subscription via the app. 2 days later, over £100 was taken out of my bank account, leaving me over drawn and panicking. I reached out to mad muscle and explained this. Going back and forth via e mail with them flatly refusing to give me a refund left me mentally drained, not to mention broke! They don’t care about your wellbeing - they care about tricking you into taking large amounts of money out of your bank! Just avoid it at all costs!

reviews.title: The only thing mad is how basic this app is
reviews.text:
Only worth getting for absolutely newbies to exercise. The pathways are very basic. The instructors take two minutes to explain an exercise, by which time you’ve completely cooled down and lost all benefit to doing it in the first place. You’ll have twenty seconds of squats, followed by a minutes rest. 
A twenty minute session is 5 mins of warm up (of which 2 is spent warming up), ten mins of exercise, most of which is the instructor laboriously explaining the most basic aspect whilst you lose you heart rate, then a five minute cooldown.
Absolutely pointless for anyone wanting to get in shape. There are far better apps out there than this

I then heard nothing more until the day my trial expired when I got the message “how’s the program and meal plan coming along?” I questioned this only to receive an automated reply to renew my subscription at another £49.99 a month. So download the app use the basic workouts to follow along if you are new to training or just want to follow something but that’s all I’d recommend. I have 30 years martial arts and gym experience and can honestly say you will not get shredded in 28 days like the ads seem to claim. You will get a bit fitter and probably do enough to live a bit longer if you do no exercise but don’t expect a miracle. I wanted to begin my workouts at the beginning of a month and purchased this plan ahead of time.  You can go back and choose that workout from the calendar date and perform it, but the credit goes in the past not when you perform the workout. Forget about support or asking a single question unless you purchase one of the more advanced plans, and even then, I am not sure if it exists.  It’s a shame, I would have liked to try this and see how it goes.

reviews.title: Caveat Empor
reviews.text: As with other users of this app, I can only conclude that this is a scam. What seemed an interesting resource to improve fitness turned out to be nothing more than a resource for fleecing users. The complicated and confusing set-up process ensures you sign up for useless extras. Attempts at cancellation prove challenging and the terms and conditions ensure refunds are virtually impossible to secure. The scale of the charges offers poor value for money. It’s a pity Apple allows apps like this to operate. There once vaunted ethics have gone the way of the Dodo. They are more interested in their 30% than in protecting consumers. This app experience has been a powerful learning experience.

reviews.title: Deceptive TOS “Autorenew Hell”
reviews.text: You will likely spend the time when you could have been exercising at the gym trying to cancel your subscription to MM. Language and navigation around the account is unclear regarding when and how often they will continue to autorenew. I don’t trust companies that play this game because even if you alert them the second the charge hits your account (which is how I learned this account had not been cancelled), MM support tells you it’s “too late” but offers complimentary extension to the service/subscription you no longer want. This tactic allows them to charge you again after the “courtesy extension” expires hoping youve forgotten to delete the account again. Update: I’m not sure if the response below is automated or not, but I didn’t post my review until *after* I had gone multiple rounds with your customer support. Offering me extra months on a subscription I did not want renewed in the first place is hardly a positive customer solution and telling me seconds after the charge is posted it’s “too late” is also a bad practice. Maybe stop deleting negative feedback on your socials too? Just a thought.

reviews.text: I wish I had read the one star reviews before signing up to a discounted trial period.  The product itself is fine, the subscription process is disingenuous at best.  The fact there is no email notification when they are about to take payment suggests a business model that is dependent on fools like me who have stopped using the app but failed to notice the payments still being taken.  I have just cancelled my subscription and only hope that I don’t suffer the same poor service that other 1 star respondents have submitted.  Claims from MM that ‘pricing is clear’ on the app is not born out by the many people complaining.  It may not be fraudulent or an illegal scam but it is definitely taking advantage of their customers.  I hope they feel clever and good about themselves.

Не рекомендую это приложение. Цена заявлена одна, но когда ты подтверждаешь план тренировки с тебя списывают ещё дополнительно 49.99€ 
На возврат средств предлагают продлить подписку на 3 месяца, но возврат денег не производят.

reviews.title: BEWARE! Money Grab.
reviews.text: First off, they are vague about the features of the app and don’t provide a trial period, so you have to roll the dice and hope it’s what you want. During the information taking process, you must confirm everything, but once you do that and they have your information, that’s when it begins. You select something think ng you’re exploring, and you now have a new $60 charge to your card for something you never approved or confirmed, and the will not refund you. The app has two options for location: gym or home, but they don’t allow for a home gym or imagine that you may have one, like I do, so they either assume you are working out with nothing (home) or everything (gym) and you can’t choose the equipment you actually have (I have a lot, but not everything). I warn you to beware. This app is not what you might think and there is no way to get your money back, if you get caught. I don’t need a personal nutritionist , but I now have one for 4 months. I hope they never make another dollar. They are predators.

reviews.title: Be very careful
reviews.text:
Everything around this app is built to silently upsell you, so once you think you have purchased the app, “continue” doesn’t mean go to the app you purchased. It means add this on as an additional purchase. And there is no confirming that this additional thing is what you wanted. The money is just immediately removed from your account. 
Upon contacting them, I was told that I won’t get a refund, instead I will get 3 more months. That way, they can feel good about handling a complaint and keep the money on their books. So be careful in dealing with the company.
The app itself is ok, probably worth the “sale” price. Definitely not worth full price. Learning a new skill (tai chi) and there is no breakdown of the movement. It demonstrates the movement and the voice over gives vague descriptions. But things are happening with multiple body parts moving at the same time. It would be nice to isolate a movement and get comfortable with that. Then isolate a different body part, then put it all together. Also, there have been occurrences where the voice over didn’t match the video… very amateurish.

reviews.title: Please look elsewhere
reviews.text:
I was running on the treadmill and an add for MadMuscles popped up. I have been looking for an additional workout other than running and weights and have always been interested in Tai Chi. After clicking on the link there were multiple questions to gauge fitness level and what my goals are. After spending roughly 5 minutes answering questions I then had to put in my email to get my results. There was then a “special offer” that would expire if I did not act now! You do not have time to research the company but it said there was a “30 day money back guarantee” so I did it. I was extremely disappointed. The Tai Chi videos are not well done and there is little explanation on how to do them. Essentially the video plays and shows the moves and then rewinds and goes through the workout. If you have no experience in Tai Chi you will find this very challenging. 
  The very unfortunate next encounter was with their customer support. They continue to try to get you to stay offering additional discounts. What I did not realize is the app automatically renews your subscription and the price goes up to $60 per month for the basic service. However I was still within my 30 day window and the customer service representative was completely unhelpful. Even though I signed up to workout three times a week, she told me I need to work out 14 days in a row, prove that I had done so and then they would “review my application” and see if a refund would be provided. Their pressure tactics get you to

reviews.title: Bad business
reviews.text: I knowingly downloaded and purchased this app to explore it. I chose the free trial service. I wanted to give it a real try. But when I logged into the app, it very sneakily asked me if I wanted to add some additional options. I could not proceed to anything else on the app unless I decided. I accidentally hit the button… I hoped it would just add to a cart that I could then delete. No, it actually automatically signed me up for that extra feature and charged me $50. It did not even ask me to confirm payment the way the original payment was done. I went back-and-forth with their customer support looking for a refund of the $50 service. And all they kept offering me were additional services that I did not want. Be careful when you use this app! Before you know it, you’ll be clicking and adding $1000 worth of services. I was so disgusted. I deleted the app altogether and refuse to use even the service I paid for. I’ll be fighting this with my bank.

reviews.title: Good but not what I signed up for
reviews.text:
I originally downloaded the app for the short, effective workouts — the 7–9 minute sessions were perfect and really made me feel the muscles working. But after a while, all the short workouts disappeared.

I contacted customer service and was told it was due to the type of workout I’d selected, but nothing on my end had changed. Suddenly only long workouts were available, across every section of the app and every exercise type.

Because of this, I stopped using the app and went back to my previous fitness app - I won’t be renewing

reviews.title: Stay away! I requested a refund the next day, but had to fight them for 3 days to get it👎
reviews.text: The exercises seem ok, but definitely could be better. Specifically the exercises should be explained by the instructor, not via voiceover. But the worst part is the insistent upselling. They send emails which seem to share helpful information but once you open the link it’s just a sales pitch to spend more money on coaching, meals, and/or exercise programs that should already be included in the original subscription. Very annoying, frustrating and lead me to perusing a refund.  I requested my refund 24 hours after my payment but had to fight via email (they don’t have phone or chat support) for an additional two days to get them to honor the refund. They offered 25%, then 40%, then as a ‘special exception’ 50%. Finally I confrontation them with the federal cooling-off rule that gives consumers 3 days to cancel a purchase and receive a full refund and they processed the full refund.   Very shady business practices imo.

reviews.title: Fraudsters - avoid at all costs
reviews.text:
This company is operating dishonestly and probably fraudulently. They take your money for a ‘trial’, and even if you cancel then they will still direct debit your account. They have just taken £84 from my account despite me cancelling almost immediately after signing up, and refusing to acknowledge the cancellation or refund my money. 
I have now commenced action through UK small claims process and will keep fighting them for every penny back plus costs. Whatever you do, do not give this company any money.
Also, ignore their copy/paste responses to negative reviews - they have no intention of helping or refunding your money. These people are fraudsters, pure and simple.

reviews.title: Broken hopes.
reviews.text: Be careful with these guys. If you sign up for a trial period, immediately go to the special menu item and make sure you've canceled your subscription. And don't confirm that you want additional services like nutrition advice or anything else unless you're 100% sure you're willing to pay extra for them. Otherwise, the seller will happily charge you extra without prior notice. This is a business that borders on decency. I didn't feel like the provider was committed to building long-term, trusting relationships with its clients. The idea is very good, and the platform's implementation is almost satisfactory. But instead of improving quality, the owner focused on increasing cash flow. I tried to become a regular customer twice. There won't be a third time.

reviews.title: Just another con.
reviews.text: Was advertised by a woman claiming to understand us women of a certain age and actually stating that we don’t need exercise advice from men. Offered a four week plan. But sadly, typical app of overwhelming options, no clear plan, and not a woman in sight. Secondly, £10 for four weeks, fair. Then an additional £2 VAT. Okay can live with that. Checked the whole of that page for subscription info as did not want them. Nothing mentioned. Once in and logged on, oh look, you have a renewal in a month for £50!!! Cancel it and it just spins saying updating when anything else would be instant. Total con, another app taking advantage of women looking for help and answers in a confusing, menopausal world. I await my refund and cancellation.
